abstract: Perceptual audio codecs often use predictive coding to further reduce signal redundancy. Rather than learning the entire codec pipeline end-to-end, we insert a small neural network as a drop-in, deterministic predictor in an otherwise conventional codec: the network estimates the next Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT) coefficient block from a short context of reconstructed blocks, and the encoder transmits the quantized residual. We compare Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predictors against a non-predictive baseline and a per-line Normalized Least Mean Squares (NLMS) linear predictor (similar to the MPEG-2 AAC Main Profile predictor). The CNN consistently outperforms the MLP, the linear predictor, and the baseline in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), noise-to-mask ratio (NMR), and MUSHRA evaluation scores. Using a 512-sample analysis window (w = 512), our neural predictors recover, and the CNN exceeds, the coded quality obtained by the non-predictive baseline after quadrupling the analysis-window length to w = 2048, at substantially lower algorithmic delay. The CNN uses only 0.13M parameters (roughly 20x fewer than the MLP) and has a decoder real-time factor (RTF) of ~0.10 on a consumer CPU.

oneSentenceThesis: 论文把多层感知机或卷积网络作为确定性预测器插入常规 MDCT 感知编码的残差路径，用已重建系数块预测当前块并只传量化残差，在 512 点短窗下以约 0.13M 参数的卷积模型取得优于线性预测和长窗基线的信噪比、噪声掩蔽比和主观分，代价是编码端选带开销增大而解码仍远快于实时。
originalTitle: Lightweight Neural Prediction for MDCT-Based Perceptual Audio Coding
readerTitle: 在短窗 MDCT 编码里加一个小神经网络预测器
